name: Emergent
summary: AI app builder. Describe what you want and Emergent builds full-stack web apps for you — an agentic, credit-based platform that turns prompts into working software with no manual coding.
best_for: founders, PMs and builders who want to turn a prompt into a working full-stack web app or MVP fast, without writing the code themselves
skip_if: you need a hardened, security-audited production system with no human review, or your usage would burn through credits faster than the value returns
honest_knock: The real cost is credit consumption, not the flat sticker -- a genuinely complex app burns 10-20+ credits per big change, so serious builders move up tiers faster than the price list implies. Now do the division, because Emergent's own pricing page doesn't. Standard is $20 for 100 credits, so 20 cents a credit. Pro is $200 for 750, which is 26.7 cents. Moving up a tier makes every unit of work more expensive, not less: Pro costs 33% more per credit than Standard, and annual billing keeps the gap (17 cents against 22.3). That is the opposite of the volume discount the ladder looks like -- you are buying a 1M-token context window, custom agents and priority support, not cheaper work. And there is nowhere cheap to go above it: Business and Enterprise are both quote-only, so passing 750 credits a month means a sales call rather than a bigger plan. Check what your month actually needs before you upgrade; one Standard month plus purchased extra credits may beat one Pro month. AI-generated code still needs a human eye: review it for security, correctness and maintainability before anything touches real users.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-08-31 on emergent.sh/pricing) Free $0 (10 credits/mo); Standard $20/mo, or $17/mo billed annually, for 100 credits (the page states a $36 annual saving, 15%); Pro $200/mo, or $167/mo billed annually, for 750 credits (a $396 saving, 16.5%). Above Pro the ladder is quote-only: Business and Enterprise both show 'Custom' and route to Book a demo, adding RBAC, SSO, shared workspaces and co-editing (Business) and user-level credit limits, audit logs, self-hosted database support, VPC deployment and priority SLAs (Enterprise). The $300/mo Team tier with 1,250 shared credits is no longer offered. Credits meter the work -- simple changes 1-2, medium features 5-10, complex refactors 10-20+ -- which comes from earlier research and was not re-confirmed on the 31 Aug read of the pricing page.

sessions.what: On 26 September 2026 we built the same class-booking web app in Lovable, Replit and Emergent from one identical prompt, each on its free plan, and checked every result against 18 tests we wrote down before the first build. We changed no code: the builder only got our prompt and, where a test failed, a repair prompt in fixed words.
findings: Emergent asked five clarifying questions before starting (we let it choose), used a separate design agent and testing agent, and had a working preview in about nine minutes.
The first version let ten simultaneous bookings into an eight-spot class, put the admin password in the CSV export link, saved a name made only of spaces and was 494 px wide on a 390 px phone screen.

The first repair fixed three of those four. While clearing test data it removed every booking in the app, ours included, and with it the database index its capacity fix relied on, so overbooking still happened. The second repair added a lock and held at eight; it removed all bookings again while cleaning up.
On the free plan the app could not be published: 'Deploy Your App' opens the plan chooser (a $1 seven-day Standard trial, then $20 a month). The two repairs used 19.17 credits, from 34.66 to 15.49.
sessions.not_tested: One run on one day, tested on the preview because publishing needs a paid plan, so whether data survives a redeploy could not be checked. Not a security audit or a load test.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
